name: Graph Anomaly Detection
problem_statement: Rank graph entities by how strongly their declared structural or temporal features deviate from a specified normality reference.

normalization: Use identical normalization for target and reference data.
Preserve fields required by feature definitions.
Do not merge parallel temporal events when event multiplicity is a feature.

problem_inputs.name: feature_definitions
problem_inputs.description: Structural, attribute, or temporal measurements used to characterize each entity.

problem_inputs.name: normality_reference
problem_inputs.description: Reference population, graph, time range, labels, or baseline statistics defining normal behavior.

problem_inputs.name: scoring_definition
problem_inputs.description: Exact rule or trained-model reference that maps entity features to a comparable anomaly score.

problem_inputs.name: candidate_entities
problem_inputs.description: Entities to score; null means every eligible entity of anomaly_target.

required_outputs.name: ranked_anomalies
required_outputs.description: Entity identity, anomaly score, rank, and resolved target type.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether all eligible candidate entities were scored before top-k selection.

optional_outputs.name: feature_values
optional_outputs.description: Resolved feature vector for returned anomalies.

optional_outputs.name: feature_contributions
optional_outputs.description: Available per-feature contribution to the score.

optional_outputs.name: supporting_subgraph
optional_outputs.description: Local evidence subgraph used to explain a returned anomaly.

optional_outputs.name: evaluation_against_labels
optional_outputs.description: Precision, recall, average precision, or ROC-AUC when trusted anomaly labels exist.

solution_semantics.objective: Compute the declared anomaly score for every eligible entity and return the highest-ranked entities.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exactness means faithful feature and score computation; an anomaly score is relative to normality_reference, not universal ground truth.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each eligible entity appears at most once.
solution_semantics.ordering: Descending anomaly score with a stable entity-ID tie break.

validation_rules: Every returned entity exists and matches anomaly_target.
Features recompute from the normalized graph and reference.
Scores reproduce from feature values and scoring_definition within tolerance.
Ranks follow score and tie policy.
edge_cases: An empty candidate population returns no anomalies.
All entities may tie under a constant or uninformative scoring definition.
Reference and target populations must not be mixed accidentally when temporal leakage matters.
